p: Smaller cinemas like this one are a joy in their own way. There's less queuing, less walking and less of the faff you get at a giant out-of-town multiplex, which matters when you're juggling tired kids or just fancy a relaxed evening. With two screens, the programme moves quite quickly, so if there's a film you've got your heart set on, catch it sooner rather than later.
Afternoon showings in the school holidays are perfect for a rainy-day reset, and an evening screening pairs nicely with tea somewhere in town beforehand.

Newton Abbot has plenty to build around a film. Courtenay Park, near the railway station, is a pleasant green space for a stroll or a kickabout, and the town is known for Newton Abbot Racecourse, which brings a buzz on race days. Just outside town, Stover Country Park has woodland and lakeside walking with a treetop trail, and the Teign estuary heads down to the sea at Teignmouth and Shaldon, both lovely spots for a seaside wander and a bag of chips.

The railway station is on the main line, which makes the town an easy hop from Exeter, Torquay and Plymouth, so you can come in by train, catch a film and head back without worrying about the car at all.
